visual.text: OUR HAWKER CENTRE · A WORD FROM THE CLEANERS
You carried it to the table. I am 68 — will you carry it back?
Return your tray. It takes you thirty seconds and saves us a great deal more.
An elderly cleaner in a blue apron pushes a trolley stacked high with used trays and bowls. Beside her, a group of students in uniform is getting up to leave a table, their trays still on it.

We are the uncles and aunties in aprons whom you walk past every day. Most of us are older than your parents. When trays are left behind, birds get to the leftovers before we do, the next family has nowhere to sit, and we spend the lunch rush bending, lifting and wiping without a pause. When you return your tray, we can keep the tables clean instead of merely cleared.

questions.text: The webpage is written as if the cleaners themselves are speaking (‘I’, ‘we’, ‘us’). Why do you think it is written this way?

scheme.answer: So that readers see the cleaners as real people and feel for them, which makes readers more willing to return their trays.
accept: A personal appeal from the cleaners is more moving than a rule, so readers are more likely to do as they ask.

questions.text: The body text ends: ‘we can keep the tables clean instead of merely cleared’. What will the cleaners be able to do if customers return their own trays?

scheme.answer: They will have time to wipe the tables properly, instead of only rushing to take away the trays.
accept: They can concentrate on cleaning the tables thoroughly rather than just removing what customers leave behind.

scheme.answer: His small act of kindness and thanks means a great deal to her, and she looks forward to it.
accept: She appreciates being thanked and treated with respect so much that she remembers him.

questions.text: How does the picture support the question asked in the headline?

scheme.answer: It shows an elderly cleaner struggling with a heavy load while young, able students leave their trays behind, which makes readers feel that they should carry their own.
accept: The contrast between the old cleaner doing the heavy work and the students walking away makes leaving a tray look unfair.
